mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand, measured by HOUST, leads to higher corporate earnings expectations and thus increases S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when controlling for macroeconomic risk factors (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment, as reflected in PAYEMS, increases labor market confidence and boosts equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no correlation with PAYEMS changes after controlling for FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in FEDFUNDS turns positive (signaling rate hikes), it raises the cost of capital, which compresses equity discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of such triggered events (binomial test p > 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening supply-side conditions, lowering growth expectations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positively correlated with INDPRO growth (R-squared > 0.15) after controlling for macroeconomic risks (F-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer price indices (CPIAUCSL) suggest accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain higher rates and suppressing equity valuations, resulting in negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL 2m moving average > previous 2m moving average
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negatively correlated with CPIAUCSL changes (Pearson's r > -0.2) in inflationary regimes (as defined by CPIAUCSL > 3%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment (UNRATE) reduces consumer and business confidence, lowering growth forecasts and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days when UNRATE crosses 6%.5%.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in 80% of post-6.5% UNRATE crosses (binomial test p < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: Coordinated declines in both FEDFUNDS and HOUST suggest dual pressures on interest rates and demand, amplifying equity valuation adjustments and producing positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of no macro proxy change (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock (evidenced by a one-standard-deviation drop in INDPRO), firms' cost structures shift, reducing profit expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in 50% of such supply shock events (binomial test p > 0.5).
